natural: shut the door and catch the thief

meaning.en: To cut off every escape route first and then deal with a weak enemy or intruder at leisure.
meaning.zh: 先堵死对方的退路，再把弱小的敌人或入侵者彻底解决。

equivalents: trap them and finish them off

examples.zh: 警察先封锁了所有出口，准备关门捉贼。
examples.en: The police sealed all the exits first, ready to trap the suspects.

examples.zh: 对方的供货渠道已被我们控制，下一步就是关门捉贼。
examples.en: We now control their supply channels, so the next step is to close in and finish them off.

story.en: The 22nd stratagem advises surrounding and wiping out a small enemy force rather than chasing it, because pursuing a small band that is allowed to run is unprofitable.
story.zh: 《三十六计》第二十二计：“小敌困之。剥，不利有攸往。”对弱小之敌要围困歼灭，不宜让其逃走再追。

usage.en: The 22nd of the Thirty-Six Stratagems, used against a small, weak enemy that should not be left room to flee. Also used in news and business writing for a sealed-in crackdown.
usage.zh: 三十六计第二十二计，用于对付弱小的敌人，使其无路可逃。也见于新闻和商业语境，指封堵后一举解决。

natural: play the fool without going mad

meaning.en: To pretend to be slow or foolish while keeping a clear head, hiding one's real intentions until the moment is right.
meaning.zh: 表面装傻，内心清醒，借此隐藏真实意图，等待时机。

equivalents: feign foolishness to bide one's time

examples.zh: 他在会上一直假痴不癫，等对手露出破绽才出手。
examples.en: He played dumb throughout the meeting and struck only when his rival slipped up.

examples.zh: 别被他的样子骗了，他这是假痴不癫。
examples.en: Don't be fooled by his act; he's only pretending to be simple.

story.en: The 27th stratagem advises pretending to be ignorant rather than acting recklessly while really knowing: stay calm and reveal nothing, like thunder gathering unseen.
story.zh: 《三十六计》第二十七计：“宁伪作不知不为，不伪作假知妄为。静不露机，云雷屯也。”

usage.en: The 27th of the Thirty-Six Stratagems. The point is to look foolish but never to lose one's senses: play dumb, stay sharp. Slightly literary; the Thirty-Six Stratagems wording is 假痴不癫.
usage.zh: 三十六计第二十七计，要点是装傻而不真疯，表面糊涂，心里明白。略带书面色彩。

literal: go up · roof · pull away · ladder
natural: lure them up the roof, then pull away the ladder

meaning.en: To tempt someone into a position, then remove their means of retreat so that they are trapped.
meaning.zh: 故意给对方留下便利，诱其深入，再切断退路，使其陷入困境。

equivalents: cut off the line of retreat

examples.zh: 他们先放出甜头，等我们投入资金，再上屋抽梯，让我们无路可退。
examples.en: They dangled the bait, and once we had invested, they pulled the ladder away so that we couldn't retreat.

examples.zh: 这是个上屋抽梯的圈套，千万别上当。
examples.en: This is a trap to lure you up and cut off your retreat, so don't fall for it.

story.en: The 28th stratagem: leave the enemy an apparent chance, lure him forward, then cut off the way back so that he has no means of escape.
story.zh: 《三十六计》第二十八计：“假之以便，唆之使前，断其援应，陷之死地。”

usage.en: The 28th of the Thirty-Six Stratagems. It can be neutral as a tactic, but in daily speech it often describes a scheme that traps someone.
usage.zh: 三十六计第二十八计，作为谋略是中性，日常多指设圈套使人无路可退。

natural: blossoms on a bare tree

meaning.en: To make a weak force look strong by dressing it up, like tying silk flowers on a withered tree.
meaning.zh: 在弱小的力量上加以装点，使其显得强大，好像在枯树上系上假花。

equivalents: make a weak position look strong
put on a show of strength

examples.zh: 这家公司实力不强，不过是树上开花，靠包装撑场面。
examples.en: The firm isn't strong; it's dressed up to look impressive.

examples.zh: 他用树上开花的办法，让对手误以为我们兵力充足。
examples.en: He used a show of strength to make the enemy think we had plenty of troops.

story.en: The 29th stratagem: when forces are weak, make them look strong by arranging them well, like a flock of wild geese flying in formation, so that a bare tree seems to bloom.
story.zh: 《三十六计》第二十九计：“借局布势，力小势大。鸿渐于陆，其羽可用为仪也。”

usage.en: The 29th of the Thirty-Six Stratagems, 树上开花, literally 'flowers bloom on a tree'. Not to be confused with 铁树开花, which means something very rare.
usage.zh: 三十六计第二十九计。注意不要与“铁树开花”（极为罕见）混淆。

natural: the oath in the peach garden

meaning.en: The sworn brotherhood of Liu Bei, Guan Yu and Zhang Fei; by extension, friends who pledge to share life and death.
meaning.zh: 指刘备、关羽、张飞在桃园结拜为兄弟；泛指志同道合者结为生死之交。

examples.zh: 三个好友像桃园结义一样，发誓要同甘共苦。
examples.en: The three friends, like the sworn brothers of the peach garden, vowed to share good times and bad.

examples.zh: 创业时他们桃园结义，如今已是并肩二十年的老搭档。
examples.en: They swore brotherhood when they started the business and have worked side by side for twenty years.

story.en: Liu Bei, Guan Yu and Zhang Fei meet and swear brotherhood in a peach garden, vowing: 'We do not ask to be born on the same day, only to die on the same day.'
story.zh: 三人在桃园焚香结拜，誓言：“不求同年同月同日生，只愿同年同月同日死。”

usage.en: From the opening chapter of 《三国演义》. Often shortened to 桃园三结义; used for close, loyal bonds between friends or business partners.
usage.zh: 出自《三国演义》第一回，也说“桃园三结义”，形容情同手足的朋友或搭档。

natural: the burning of Red Cliff

meaning.en: The decisive battle in which Zhou Yu and Zhuge Liang defeated Cao Cao's much larger fleet by fire; a model of a weak side beating a strong one by strategy.
meaning.zh: 指周瑜、诸葛亮用火攻大败曹操大军的赤壁之战；比喻以弱胜强的奇谋。

equivalents: beat a larger enemy by fire and cunning

examples.zh: 小公司靠一次精准营销，打出了火烧赤壁式的翻身仗。
examples.en: The small firm turned things around with one well-aimed campaign, like Red Cliff in miniature.

examples.zh: 电影《赤壁》讲的就是火烧赤壁的故事。
examples.en: The film 'Red Cliff' tells the story of the burning of Red Cliff.

story.en: In the winter of AD 208 Huang Gai's feigned surrender brought fire ships alongside Cao Cao's chained fleet; an east wind spread the flames and wrecked it.
story.zh: 黄盖诈降，火船乘东南风冲入曹营，连环战船尽被烧毁，曹操大败。

usage.en: In 《三国演义》 the fire attack succeeds because Zhuge Liang 'borrows the east wind'. Used for brilliant underdog victories.
usage.zh: 小说中诸葛亮借东风助火攻成功。多比喻以少胜多、以弱胜强的漂亮仗。

natural: raising havoc in Heaven

meaning.en: To wreak havoc in a place; originally the Monkey King's rebellion against the Jade Emperor's court.
meaning.zh: 原指孙悟空在天宫造反；比喻在某处大吵大闹，把秩序搅乱。

examples.zh: 孩子们在客厅里大闹天宫，把沙发垫都扔到了地上。
examples.en: The children raised hell in the living room and threw the sofa cushions on the floor.

examples.zh: 这只猫昨晚在厨房大闹天宫，打碎了两个盘子。
examples.en: The cat went on the rampage in the kitchen last night and broke two plates.

story.en: Sun Wukong, angry at being given a minor post, steals the Queen Mother's peaches and Laozi's elixir and defeats the heavenly army until the Buddha subdues him.
story.zh: 孙悟空不满弼马温之职，偷吃蟠桃仙丹，大败天兵天将，最后被如来佛祖压在五行山下。

usage.en: From 《西游记》 chapters 4 to 7, where Sun Wukong steals the peaches and elixir and fights the heavenly army. Humorous when used of messy, noisy people.
usage.zh: 出自《西游记》第四至七回。用于形容吵闹捣乱，带诙谐口吻。

natural: scrape the bone to cure poison

meaning.en: To endure terrible pain calmly for the sake of a cure; today also to carry out thorough, painful reform to remove a deep-seated problem.
meaning.zh: 形容忍受极大痛苦以治病；今多比喻下决心彻底清除积弊，不惜自我“割肉”。

equivalents: bite the bullet and cut out the rot

examples.zh: 关羽刮骨疗毒时仍谈笑饮酒，令人佩服。
examples.en: Guan Yu kept chatting and drinking while his bone was scraped, which is awe-inspiring.

examples.zh: 要根治行业乱象，就得刮骨疗毒，不能只做表面文章。
examples.en: To cure the industry's ills we need radical surgery, not window-dressing.

story.en: Guan Yu is hit by a poisoned arrow; the surgeon Hua Tuo scrapes the poison from the bone while Guan Yu calmly plays chess and drinks.
story.zh: 关羽右臂中毒箭，华佗为他刮骨去毒，关羽一面饮酒下棋，一面谈笑自若。

usage.en: Both literal (Guan Yu's story) and figurative; the figurative sense is common in news about rooting out corruption or fixing a company's culture.
usage.zh: 既指关羽的故事，又比喻彻底整治，常见于反腐和整顿的报道。

natural: three attacks on the White Bone Demon

meaning.en: Sun Wukong's three attempts to kill a demon that kept disguising itself; used for seeing through a disguise, or for being blamed while doing the right thing.
meaning.zh: 孙悟空三次识破并打死变化多端的白骨精；常比喻识破伪装，或比喻好心被误解、受冤枉。

equivalents: do right and be blamed for it

examples.zh: 他总能识破骗子的伪装，像孙悟空三打白骨精。
examples.en: He always sees through a con artist's disguise, just like Sun Wukong against the White Bone Demon.

examples.zh: 明明是为了她好，却像三打白骨精一样，反被误会了。
examples.en: I meant it for her own good, yet like Wukong with the demon, I was misunderstood.

story.en: The White Bone Demon tries three times to trick the Tang monk by disguising herself as a girl, her mother and her father; Wukong kills each form but the monk, deceived, banishes him.
story.zh: 白骨精三次变化欲骗唐僧，均被悟空打死，唐僧肉眼凡胎，反责怪悟空，将他逐走。

usage.en: From 《西游记》 chapter 27. The demon appears as a girl, an old woman and an old man; the Tang monk believes the demon, not Wukong, and sends Wukong away. There is also a 歇后语 beginning 孙悟空三打白骨精.
usage.zh: 出自《西游记》第二十七回：白骨精先后变成少女、老妇、老翁，唐僧不辨真伪，反把悟空赶走。另有歇后语“孙悟空三打白骨精”。

natural: the journey west to fetch the scriptures

meaning.en: The monk Xuanzang's pilgrimage to India for Buddhist texts; figuratively, a long, hard quest for the real thing.
meaning.zh: 指唐僧师徒前往印度取得佛经的艰难旅程；比喻历尽艰辛去追求真经、真本事。

equivalents: a pilgrimage in search of truth

examples.zh: 这次培训像西天取经，大家都盼着学回真本事。
examples.en: This training is like a pilgrimage for scriptures; everyone hopes to come back with real skills.

examples.zh: 他远赴海外学习，算是现代的西天取经。
examples.en: He went abroad to study, a modern version of fetching the scriptures.

story.en: Tripitaka and his disciples Wukong, Bajie and Sha Seng travel west to the Thunder Monastery for scriptures, overcoming demons and hardships along the way.
story.zh: 唐僧带领悟空、八戒、沙僧西行，历经九九八十一难，到天竺取得真经。

usage.en: The 《西游记》 story is based on the real monk Xuanzang (602–664), who travelled to India in the Tang dynasty. Often used of going far to study with the best teachers.
usage.zh: 《西游记》故事以唐代玄奘西行求法为蓝本。多用于远赴他乡拜师求学。

pinyin: jiǔ jiǔ bā shí yī nàn
natural: the eighty-one ordeals

meaning.en: The full set of hardships that the pilgrims had to endure in 《西游记》; used for a very long series of trials.
meaning.zh: 指唐僧师徒取经路上必须经历的全部磨难；泛指接连不断的重重难关。

examples.zh: 创业路上要闯过九九八十一难，才能见到成果。
examples.en: Founding a business means passing through eighty-one ordeals before there are results.

examples.zh: 为了办这张签证，他过了九九八十一难。
examples.en: To get this visa he went through endless hoops.

story.en: The Bodhisattva checks the register of trials and finds the pilgrims have suffered eighty, one short of the destined 'nine times nine', and has one more arranged.
story.zh: 观音检阅难簿，见唐僧师徒只历八十难，尚缺一难，遂令再生一难，凑成九九之数。

usage.en: In 《西游记》 chapter 99 the Bodhisattva finds the register one trial short and arranges another so that the total is 九九八十一. Nine is the largest single digit, so 81 means 'a great many'.
usage.zh: 《西游记》第九十九回，观音查点灾难簿，缺一难，遂补足九九八十一难。九为数之极，八十一即“极多”。

natural: Wu Song fights the tiger

meaning.en: Wu Song's feat of killing a man-eating tiger with his bare fists; used for great courage and strength.
meaning.zh: 武松在景阳冈赤手空拳打死老虎；形容英勇无畏、力大过人。

examples.zh: 他孤身制服了三名歹徒，被称为现代武松打虎。
examples.en: He subdued three criminals single-handed and was dubbed a modern Wu Song.

examples.zh: 小时候我最爱看武松打虎的连环画。
examples.en: As a child I loved the comic strip of Wu Song fighting the tiger.

story.en: Wu Song, drunk on the Jingyang Ridge, breaks his staff against a tiger and then beats it to death with his fists.
story.zh: 武松在景阳冈喝醉酒后遇虎，棒折，只好赤手空拳将虎打死。

usage.en: From 《水浒传》 chapter 23: drunk, Wu Song breaks his staff on the tiger and finishes it with his fists. There is also a 歇后语 “武松打虎——艺高人胆大”.
usage.zh: 出自《水浒传》第二十三回，武松醉后在景阳冈用拳打死老虎。另有歇后语“武松打虎——艺高人胆大”。

literal: upside down · pull up · weeping · willow
natural: pull up a willow tree, roots and all

meaning.en: Lu Zhishen's feat of uprooting a willow with his bare hands; used for immense strength.
meaning.zh: 鲁智深赤手将垂杨柳连根拔起；形容力气极大。

equivalents: pull up a tree by the roots

examples.zh: 他是个大力士，仿佛有倒拔垂杨柳的力气。
examples.en: He is so strong he seems able to pull up a willow by the roots.

examples.zh: 别看她瘦，干起活来真有倒拔垂杨柳的架势。
examples.en: She may be slim, but she works as if she could uproot a tree.

story.en: At the Great Xiangguo Monastery, Lu Zhishen grasps a willow tree, twists his body and pulls it out, roots and all, to the amazement of the rogues watching him.
story.zh: 鲁智深在大相国寺菜园，抱住垂杨柳，腰一用力，连根拔起，惊呆了众泼皮。

usage.en: From 《水浒传》 chapter 7. There is also a 歇后语 “鲁智深倒拔垂杨柳——力大无穷”. Usually humorous or admiring.
usage.zh: 出自《水浒传》第七回。另有歇后语“鲁智深倒拔垂杨柳”。多含赞叹或诙谐。

natural: seize the birthday convoy by cunning

meaning.en: The outlaws' plan to take a convoy of birthday gifts by trickery rather than force; used for winning through intelligence.
meaning.zh: 晁盖、吴用等用计劫取大名府押运的生辰礼物；比喻靠智谋而非蛮力取胜。

examples.zh: 谈判桌上，他们智取生辰纲，不费一兵一卒拿下了合同。
examples.en: At the negotiating table they won the contract by wit alone.

examples.zh: 这个游戏的关卡要像智取生辰纲一样动脑筋才能通过。
examples.en: You need to use your wits to get through this level, like the heist of the birthday convoy.

story.en: Chao Gai, Wu Yong and others pose as date merchants, drug the guards' wine and carry off the birthday gifts being sent to Cai Jing.
story.zh: 晁盖、吴用等扮作贩枣客商，用蒙汗药酒迷倒押送官兵，夺走送给蔡太师的生辰礼物。

usage.en: From 《水浒传》 chapter 16. Note 纲 is read gāng (a convoy of goods). Used playfully for cunning plans.
usage.zh: 出自《水浒传》第十六回。“纲”读 gāng，指成批运送的货物。多用于戏称巧计。

natural: Daiyu buries the fallen flowers

meaning.en: Lin Daiyu's burial of fallen petals; stands for delicate sentimentality and sorrow at fading beauty.
meaning.zh: 林黛玉埋葬落花；形容多愁善感，伤春悲秋。

examples.zh: 看她对着落叶发呆，真像黛玉葬花。
examples.en: Seeing her stare at the fallen leaves, she was just like Daiyu burying the flowers.

examples.zh: 这幅画画的是黛玉葬花，画面凄美。
examples.en: The painting of Daiyu burying the flowers is hauntingly beautiful.

story.en: Lin Daiyu gathers fallen petals into a silk bag and buries them in a mound, singing the lament 'Burying Flowers'.
story.zh: 林黛玉把落花装入锦囊，埋在花冢，吟唱《葬花吟》。

usage.en: From 《红楼梦》 chapter 27, where she sings the 《葬花吟》. Often used for lovers of melancholy, sometimes teasingly.
usage.zh: 出自《红楼梦》第二十七回，黛玉作《葬花吟》。常用来形容感伤的人，有时带调侃。

pinyin: bái máng máng dà dì zhēn gān jìng
literal: white · vast · vast · great · earth · truly · clean
natural: the great white earth, truly clean

meaning.en: Everything ends in emptiness, like snow covering the land; the final ruin of great families in 《红楼梦》.
meaning.zh: 一切归于空无，像大雪覆盖大地；指富贵之家终至败落、一无所有。

equivalents: nothing left but a blank white landscape

examples.zh: 那个显赫一时的家族，最后真是白茫茫大地真干净。
examples.en: That once-mighty family ended with nothing left at all.

examples.zh: 读到“白茫茫大地真干净”，我只觉得一阵凄凉。
examples.en: Reading 'the great white earth, truly clean', I felt only desolation.

story.en: In the song 'Birds Fly to Their Forests', the vision of the Illusory Realm ends with: 'Like a vast white earth, truly clean.'
story.zh: 《飞鸟各投林》曲末：“落了片白茫茫大地真干净！”

usage.en: The last line of the song 《飞鸟各投林》 in 《红楼梦》 chapter 5, a prophecy of the fall of the great families. Literary, used for total collapse.
usage.zh: 出自《红楼梦》第五回《飞鸟各投林》曲，预示贾府等大家族败落。书面语，指彻底衰败。

pinyin: jì shēng yú hé shēng liàng
literal: since · gave birth to · Yu · why · give birth to · Liang
natural: Since Heaven made Yu, why make Liang?

meaning.en: A lament of envy at a rival who is just as good: if I exist, why must you exist too?
meaning.zh: 对旗鼓相当的对手心怀嫉妒的慨叹：既然有了我，为什么还要有你？

equivalents: Why did heaven make you as well as me?
having a rival of equal ability

examples.zh: 他输给了同门师弟，忍不住感叹既生瑜何生亮。
examples.en: Beaten by his junior from the same school, he couldn't help sighing 'why must there be you too?'

examples.zh: 两位球星一直互相压制，球迷常说他们是既生瑜何生亮。
examples.en: The two stars always held each other back, so fans call them an 'if Yu, why Liang' pair.

story.en: The dying Zhou Yu, tormented by Zhuge Liang's outplaying him, cries to heaven three times: 'Since Heaven made Yu, why did it make Liang?'
story.zh: 周瑜被诸葛亮气得箭疮迸裂，仰天长叹：“既生瑜，何生亮！”连叫数声而亡。

usage.en: The usual form is 既生瑜，何生亮, with a comma, said by the dying Zhou Yu in 《三国演义》. Quoted with irony about rivalries, or to express jealousy.
usage.zh: 通常写作“既生瑜，何生亮”。多用于调侃强劲的对手，或表达嫉妒。

pinyin: fú bù qǐ de ā dǒu
natural: an Adou who cannot be propped up

meaning.en: A hopelessly incompetent person who cannot be helped however much support he is given.
meaning.zh: 指无论怎样扶持，也不能成器的无能之人。

equivalents: someone you can't do anything with

examples.zh: 你再怎么帮他，他也是扶不起的阿斗。
examples.en: However much you help him, he's a lost cause.

examples.zh: 别把希望寄托在扶不起的阿斗身上。
examples.en: Don't pin your hopes on someone who cannot be propped up.

usage.en: Adou is the childhood name of Liu Shan, Liu Bei's weak son and the second ruler of Shu Han, famous in 《三国演义》 for 乐不思蜀. Insulting; not for use to someone's face.
usage.zh: 阿斗是刘备之子刘禅的小名，《三国演义》中以无能、乐不思蜀著称。含贬义，不宜当面说。

text: 宁教我负天下人，休教天下人负我
pinyin: níng jiào wǒ fù tiān xià rén, xiū jiào tiān xià rén fù wǒ
literal: rather · let · I · betray · world · people, never · let · world · people · betray · me
natural: better I betray the world than the world betray me

meaning.en: A ruthless, selfish creed: I would rather wrong everyone else than let anyone wrong me.
meaning.zh: 极端自私冷酷的信条：宁可我对不起天下人，也不许天下人对不起我。

equivalents: better I wrong others than they wrong me

examples.zh: 他信奉宁教我负天下人，休教天下人负我，难怪没有朋友。
examples.en: He lives by 'better I betray the world than be betrayed', no wonder he has no friends.

examples.zh: 这种宁教我负天下人，休教天下人负我的想法太危险了。
examples.en: The creed of 'better I wrong everyone else' is too dangerous.

story.en: After mistakenly killing Lü Boshe's family, Cao Cao says to Chen Gong: 'I would rather betray all under heaven than let all under heaven betray me.'
story.zh: 曹操误杀吕伯奢一家后，对陈宫说：“宁教我负天下人，休教天下人负我！”

usage.en: A line that sums up Cao Cao's villainous side in 《三国演义》. Mostly quoted to criticise selfish, treacherous people.
usage.zh: 《三国演义》里曹操的名言，概括其奸雄本色。多用来批评自私背信的人。

text: 山中方七日，世上已千年
pinyin: shān zhōng fāng qī rì, shì shàng yǐ qiān nián
variants: 洞中方七日，世上已千年
literal: mountain · in · only · seven · days, world · on · already · thousand · years
natural: seven days in the mountains, a thousand years in the world

meaning.en: Time passes differently in the fairy realm: a short stay there equals centuries among mortals.
meaning.zh: 仙境中的时间过得很慢，在山中只过了几天，人间已是千年。

equivalents: a few days there, centuries here

examples.zh: 读了“山中方七日，世上已千年”的故事，我才理解什么叫时间错位。
examples.en: After reading the tale of 'seven days in the mountains, a thousand years in the world', I understood what time displacement means.

examples.zh: 度假回来像是山中方七日，世上已千年，手机上的新闻都变了。
examples.en: Back from holiday, it felt like 'seven days in the mountains, a thousand years in the world'; all the news had changed.

usage.en: Folk wording of the 'rotten axe handle' legend (烂柯): the woodcutter Wang Zhi watches two immortals play chess and finds when he returns that generations have passed. Also said 洞中方七日，世上已千年.
usage.zh: 民间流传的“烂柯”故事：樵夫王质观仙人下棋，回家时已历数代。亦作“洞中方七日，世上已千年”。
